text:
mo_acme: Hey team, seeing intermittent 429s for a job that spikes for ~10s every 5 minutes. Token usage stays low but we lose a handful of requests. Any ideas?

alex_support: sorry about that — can you paste a minimal repro (curl + headers) and the x-burst-credit headers from a 429 response if available?

mo_acme: here is the curl we use from our cron, run every 5m with concurrency 6: `for i in {1..6}; do curl -sS -H \"Authorization: Bearer $KEY\" -d '{"input":"x"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate & done`

mo_acme: sample response headers when failing: `HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests`
`x-burst-credits: 0`
`x-burst-refill-since: 12`
`x-rate-limit-remaining: 0`

eli_ops: thanks. That pattern (short, high-concurrency 10s spike) can hit the smoothing logic. Are you on a shared hosted account or dedicated?

mo_acme: hosted, free trial org.

eli_ops: ok. Two likely causes: 1) fractional refill rounding + concurrent drains causes temporary negative race where multiple workers see the cushion as available and then oversubscribe; 2) smoothing window misalignment with your 10s spike so credits get consumed faster than the refill loop expects.

alex_support: can you also paste timestamps (approx) for a failure window? we want to correlate with our metrics.

mo_acme: failures happened at ~2026-03-16T14:05:10Z and 14:10:11Z, same pattern.

sre-bot: Incident note: throttles observed matching org mo_acme at 2026-03-16T14:05-14:07Z, 6 requests concurrently -> 4 succeeded 2 429s. Stack: hosted-prod-1. Linked metric: burst-credit-balance dip.

talia_eng: quick repro on our side yields the same oscillation when concurrency >=5 and spike duration < smoothing window. Two immediate mitigations: reduce concurrency in cron (3) or add a tiny jitter + ramp. That reduces simultaneous drains.

mo_acme: worried about changing concurrency, this job needs throughput. Is there a config on the Redwood side we can change?

eli_ops: yes — we can change your smoothing policy and burst ceiling for hosted accounts: options are `smoothing_window_ms` (default 15000), `burst_ceiling` (default 100 credits), and `burst_refill_rate` (credits/sec). For short spikes increase `smoothing_window_ms` to 30000 so the refill stabilizes over your spike, or increase `burst_ceiling` if you have a steady need. We'll need permission to apply org-level change.

alex_support: short-term workaround: add client-side stagger: `sleep $((RANDOM%3))` in your cron loop and switch concurrency to controlled pool so requests don't all start at once. That often fixes microburst 429s instantly.

mo_acme: any way to see why `x-burst-refill-since` is 12? seems low.

eli_ops: `x-burst-refill-since` shows seconds since last refill tick for your org. If multiple parallel processes request at nearly same time the header can show small numbers because refill hasn't advanced yet for all. We log per-org refill events, will check if your org hits rounding floor (fractional credits < 1) leading to effective zero shown.

mo_acme: could this be an off-by-one in the refill code?

talia_eng: unlikely an off-by-one, more a tradeoff between fractional refill precision and overhead. We maintain refill at 100ms granularity internally and store fractional remainder. But concurrent drains expose races especially on hosted tiers where lock contention is coarse. We're looking at improving per-org atomic update patterns next quarter.

mo_acme: timeline for a fix?

talia_eng: medium-term: better atomic updates + per-request token reservation patch in ~6-8 weeks. Short-term we can apply a config change to your org today: increase smoothing_window_ms to 30k and bump burst_ceiling to 140 for two weeks while you evaluate.

alex_support: if you want that change, I can open an org update and apply during business hours. I'll also set a temporary alert to notify us if 429 rate > 1% for the next day.

mo_acme: please do. Also can we get a recommendation on client backoff strategy?

eli_ops: use exponential backoff with jitter, cap retry attempts to 3 for these spikes. Example pseudocode: `sleep = min(2**attempt * 0.2 + random()*0.1, 2.0)` — avoids retry storms.

mo_acme: sounds good. Thanks.

sre-bot: Change request created: CHG-2026-331. Owner: alex_support. Action: apply smoothing_window_ms=30000 + burst_ceiling=140 for org mo_acme for 14 days.

alex_support: applied in staging, will schedule prod change at 2026-03-17 09:00 PST. Will post before/after metrics. :thumbsup:

mo_acme: thanks team, appreciate the quick triage. We'll monitor and report back if we still see blips.

eli_ops: follow-up note: if you prefer not to change server-side, easiest client fix is stagger+bounded concurrency + jittered retries. We'll leave the change until you confirm.

mo_acme: we'll accept the server-side change for 14 days and test.

alex_support: closing loop once we've got 24h of reduced 429s or your sign-off.

talia_eng: added a small dashboard tile for mo_acme under 'burst-credit' so Product Support can validate impact.

mo_acme: ping when live tomorrow morning, thanks everyone!
